review.summary: Fixed two blocker bugs: floating-point truncation in price conversion (int() instead of round()) caused prices like '19.99 EUR' to be stored as 1998 instead of 1999 minor units; INSERT OR REPLACE in upsert_listing triggered ON DELETE CASCADE on price_history, silently losing price history on every rescrape. Both fixes verified by the existing test suite and manual checks against the acceptance criteria.

findings.title: Floating-point truncation in price conversion
findings.description: int(parse_amount(...) * minor_unit_factor(...)) truncated due to IEEE 754: 19.99 * 100 = 1998.9999... -> 1998. REQ-1 requires exact minor-unit storage. Fixed by using round() in all three ingestion paths (upsert_listing, apply_update, import_records).

findings.title: INSERT OR REPLACE cascades delete of price history
findings.description: upsert_listing used INSERT OR REPLACE which deletes the existing row before inserting. With ON DELETE CASCADE on price_history.listing_id, every rescrape silently dropped all prior price history entries. REQ-2 requires price history is never lost. Fixed by splitting into explicit INSERT (new listing) and UPDATE (existing listing) paths.
